question:
A conducting rod of length $l$ and mass $m$ can slide without friction on two parallel horizontal conducting rails separated by distance $l$. The rails are connected to an **ideal capacitor** of capacitance $C$ (initially **uncharged**). A uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to the plane of the rails. The rod is pulled along the rails by a constant external force $F$ applied from $t=0$.

Assume the rails and contacts have **negligible resistance**, the capacitor has no leakage, and self-inductance effects are negligible. Find the (constant) acceleration $a$ of the rod.
